statement: For the defined candidate class of bilateral grade dilation constructions, the fixed canonical Gaussian common-frame instance at displacement a = 1.5 (sigma = 2.0) fails arithmetic zero descent with certified strictly positive cross-term X_{xi, W} in [0.023172135, 0.023172297] and positive second variation V_2 > 0 strictly, closing this fixed candidate instance (FIXED_GAUSSIAN_COMMON_FRAME_INSTANCE_CLOSED). Whole-class closure for general non-canonical or untuned window families remains an open classification (BILATERAL_GRADE_ROUTE_CLASS_CLOSURE_OPEN).

quantified_variables.description: Fixed candidate instance in the defined bilateral grade class

hypotheses: Fixed canonical Gaussian window W(t) = 1/sqrt(2pi) exp(-t^2/2) at a = 1.5
Certified positivity of cross-term X_{xi, W} in [0.023172135, 0.023172297] from CLM-CT-027
Strictly positive norm term 2 a^2 int W |g'|^2 dt > 0
Weighted-adjoint second variation identity: ||L_a g||_W^2 + Re<L_{a,W}^* g, L_a g>_W = 2 a^2 int W |g'|^2 dt - Re int W (1 + (W'/W)(t + ia)) g conj((t - ia) g') dt
object_studied: Fixed canonical Gaussian candidate instance of bilateral grade dilation route
multiplicity_convention: All zero multiplicities and background components included
measure_and_window: Canonical standard Gaussian probability window on R
order_of_limits: Evaluation of finite parameter instance with certified point witness
exact_conclusion: The fixed canonical Gaussian candidate instance is closed: arithmetic zero descent fails with V_2 > 0 strictly (FIXED_GAUSSIAN_COMMON_FRAME_INSTANCE_CLOSED); whole-class status for arbitrary Schwartz windows remains an open classification (BILATERAL_GRADE_ROUTE_CLASS_CLOSURE_OPEN).
logical_negation: The fixed canonical Gaussian instance achieves exact arithmetic zero descent V_2 = 0 (strictly refuted by certified positivity of V_2)
dependencies: CLM-CT-027 (Completed xi cross-term certified non-vanishing point witness)
falsification_attempts: Evaluated equality-case cancellation analysis on second variation V_2 confirming absence of zero-crossing on canonical Gaussian window
Evaluated weighted-adjoint operator L_{a,W}^* = -(t+ia) d/dt + t^2 + iat - 1 proving positive derivative term 2 a^2 int W |g'|^2 dt
Tested parameter variation over grid (a, sigma_W) confirming positivity throughout
Evaluated boundary asymptotic dominance and tail limits as a -> infinity and sigma_W -> 0
